summary: Dutchess County NY: 60-ft state fire tower built 1933, in service until 1988, decommissioned 1989; still standing on private land and closed to the public.

facts.design: 60-foot Aermotor LS-40 steel tower with observer's cabin
facts.agency: New York State Conservation Department (now the Department of Environmental Conservation)

access.note: On private property and closed to the public, per the Forest Fire Lookout Association list and Wikipedia. The list's note is undated.

events.note: Erected by the NY State Conservation Department as a steel tower with an observer's cabin completed shortly after
The first five observers were hired, collectively serving from April 1933
A 1953 notice names Oscar Ferris as fire observer on Clove Mountain
Collective service of the first five observers ended in May 1960; later staffing is not described in the sources read
Officially decommissioned as a fire lookout the year after service ended with the 1988 fire season

notes_for_editor: Height is given as 60 feet in both sources; 18.3 m is converted from feet. The 'closed to the public' status comes from the undated NYSFFLA list entry; no source gives a date, so the current condition is not confirmed on site. Wikipedia's private-property statement is a secondary claim; its own references (Laskey 2003; Starr roster) were not read. The 1953 Ferris notice is a Chronicle-Express item as quoted on Forest Lookouts and is not checked against the original. The Forest Lookouts page spells the county 'Duchess' in one place; the record and other sources use Dutchess, so no correction is proposed. Staffing after 1960 is not documented in the sources read.
